draft.title: Piecewise and step graphs
card: Piecewise graph
A piecewise graph is made of separate line segments, each with its own rule over its own range of x values. The rule changes at a set point.
Step graph
A step graph is made of horizontal segments with jumps between them. The value stays fixed over a range, then jumps to a new amount.
Open and closed dots
A closed dot means the end value is included. An open dot means it is not.
Example: a car park charges $5 for up to 1 hour, then $9 for over 1 hour up to 2 hours. A stay of exactly 1 hour costs $5. A stay of 1.5 hours costs $9.
draft.remember: Piecewise graphs change rule at set points. Step graphs hold a value, then jump.

a.q: A car park charges $4 for up to 1 hour, $7 for over 1 hour up to 2 hours, and $10 for over 2 hours up to 3 hours. What does a stay of 2.5 hours cost?
a.why: 2.5 hours is over 2 hours and up to 3 hours, so the charge is $10. The charge is not added up across steps, so $17 is wrong.
a.clue: Find which time range 2.5 hours falls in.

b.q: A step graph for a car park shows $6 for up to 2 hours, then $11 for over 2 hours up to 4 hours. Which cost applies to a stay of exactly 2 hours?
opts: $6, because the first step includes 2 hours
$11, because the next step starts at 2 hours
$8.50, the average of the two steps
b.why: The first step covers up to and including 2 hours, so the dot at 2 hours is closed on $6. The $11 step only starts just after 2 hours. A stay has one charge, not an average.
b.clue: Check which step has the closed dot at 2 hours.

b.best: $6, because the first step includes 2 hours

problems.detail: Saying a piecewise graph is made of 'separate' line segments could suggest the segments must be disconnected. Many piecewise graphs, such as tax scales, join up at the points where the rule changes.

check.summary: Both questions are correct and fair. The only issue is that 'separate line segments' on the card could wrongly suggest piecewise graphs are always disconnected.
